facts.text: Ruidoso’s name comes from the Spanish “Rio Ruidoso,” meaning “Noisy River,” a nod to the Mescalero Apache who first settled the area.
Nestled in the Sierra Blanca range, Ruidoso sits beside the 12,000‑foot Ski Apache, a popular ski resort owned by the Mescalero Apache Tribe.
The tribe also runs the Inn of the Mountain Gods resort, which features a casino, hotel, arcade, and golf course right in Ruidoso.
Ruidoso Public Library began in 1954 as a modest collection, and today occupies a 14,600‑square‑foot building with a garden, archive room, and outdoor patio.
Every summer, Ruidoso lights up with free live music nights in Midtown and the quirky Long Dog Derby, drawing music lovers and racing fans alike.
